title: Fröhlich Bipolarons in Two-Dimensional Materials
authors: A. Kudlis, V. Shahnazaryan, I. Iorsh, I. A. Shelykh, I. V. Tokatly
abstract: Motivated by the progress in the physics of two-dimensional materials and the recent two-dimensional generalization of the Fröhlich model, we study the formation of bipolarons in polar monolayers. Because of very special nonlocal dielectric screening in two dimensions, this setting differs qualitatively from the conventional Fröhlich model. In monolayers, (i) long wavelength LO phonons acquire a nontrivial dispersion; (ii) the Fröhlich electron-phonon vertex becomes momentum-dependent and regular at small momenta; and (iii) direct repulsion between charge carriers takes the Keldysh-Rytova form. Using the Feynman path-integral variational approach, we show that the region in the parameter space where stable bipolarons exist is strongly modified compared to the usual quasi-two-dimensional model with dispersionless phonons. Specifically, in the most favorable limit, when the ratio $σ_0$ of the static polarizability to the high-frequency polarizability tends to infinity, the lower critical coupling, sufficient for the formation of bipolarons, can be made arbitrarily small. More surprisingly, we demonstrate that no stable bipolarons can exist in the strong coupling limit: in the isolated monolayer the stability region is always confined to a finite range of coupling constants. In general, the stability region is strongly shifted toward large values of the polarizability ratio $σ_0$, well beyond the parameter regimes in representative crystals, which indicates that polar monolayers do not favor bipolarons.
summary: This paper theoretically examines bipolaron formation in polar two-dimensional monolayers using a variational path-integral approach. It finds that the unique 2D screening effects drastically alter the stability landscape, showing that stable bipolarons are suppressed in the strong coupling limit. This work is crucial for predicting charge transport phenomena in next-generation 2D electronic materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the formation and stability of bipolarons (pairs of charge carriers coupled to phonons) in polar monolayers, contrasting this behavior with conventional quasi-two-dimensional models.
main_result: The stability region for bipolarons is strongly modified in monolayers, showing that no stable bipolarons exist in the strong coupling limit, contrary to expectations from simpler models.
method: The analysis employs the Feynman path-integral variational approach to calculate the zero-temperature ground-state energy of the system.
model_or_system: The system models two charge carriers interacting via Fröhlich electron-phonon coupling and direct Coulomb repulsion within an isolated, polar two-dimensional monolayer environment.
key_observables: Bipolaron binding energy ($e_{bp}$), one-polaron energy ($e_{pol}$), and the critical coupling constant required for bipolaron formation.
important_parameters: The ratio of static to high-frequency polarizability ($\sigma_0$), the effective coupling parameter ($\alpha_{eff}$), and the screening lengths ($r_0, r_\infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an isolated monolayer environment, leading to specific nonlocal dielectric screening effects, and utilizes variational approximations in the path integral formalism.
figures_summary: The notes detail the derivation of energy functionals and the minimization of the energy difference between one-polaron and bipolaron states using multiple variational parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the unique physics of 2D monolayers (momentum-dependent vertices, Keldysh-Rytova repulsion) to applying the variational path-integral method to calculate the ground-state energy, culminating in the determination of the stability region.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding charge carrier interactions in modern 2D materials, which is highly relevant for designing novel quantum electronic devices.
